name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.faithful_and_compactOperatorModel_of_singleton_amongNonUnital
title: Compact-operator conclusion for the unital singleton condition

content.display_title: Compact-operator conclusion for the unital singleton condition
content.one_sentence_role: Applies the nonunital compact-operator theorem to the same operator-valued map underlying a unital representation.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital $*$-representation satisfying the singleton condition of R11. Then $\pi$ is injective and $$\pi(A)=\mathcal K(H).$$
content.assumptions: The quantified irreducible representations in the singleton condition need not initially be packaged with a unit equation; R11 shows that nonzero irreducibility forces that equation. No separability assumption is made on $A$.
content.conclusion: The same map $a\mapsto\pi(a)$ is a faithful compact-operator model. In particular, it gives a $*$-isomorphism $A\cong_*\mathcal K(H)$.
content.proof_summary: View the same operator-valued function as a representation in the unit-free interface, apply the nonunital singleton theorem, and translate its conclusions back without changing any operator.
proof_steps: Let $\pi_0$ denote the same function $a\mapsto\pi(a)$, regarded in the representation interface that does not require a unit equation: $$\pi_0(a)=\pi(a)\qquad(a\in A).$$ No operator is changed.

The hypothesis of R11 says exactly that $\pi_0$ represents the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations. Apply [Faithfulness and compact-operator model from a singleton representation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CompactModel.lean#L43-L49) to $\pi_0$.
The output is injectivity of $\pi_0$ together with $\pi_0(A)=\mathcal K(H)$. Since $\pi_0(a)=\pi(a)$ for every $a$, these are precisely injectivity of $\pi$ and $\pi(A)=\mathcal K(H)$.
